defects.label: blocker
defects.summary: Tool policy matrix makes the workflow impossible under its own rules: Intake forbids canonical writes but M1 requires canonical run_manifest/event_log + stage_handoff; Review forbids all writes but M5 requires emitting review_findings.json + stage_handoff. This violates hard-gate consistency for executable stages.

evidence.note: Intake policy restricts artifact/workspace writes to non-canonical only
M1 deliverables require canonical run_manifest/event_log and stage_handoff
Review policy denies artifact_write/workspace_write entirely
M5 deliverables require review_findings.json and stage_handoff Review→Judge
R5 requires stage_handoff at every stage transition

defects.label: blocker
defects.summary: Evidence pointer instances are non-compliant with the plan’s own declared RFC6901 evidence pointer shape. R10/AT10 define evidence pointers as {artifact_ref, entity_id|null, json_pointer, note}, but the plan’s evidence instances omit entity_id and include extra fields (candidate_id, artifact_id, quote). This would fail any strict evidence-pointer validator and breaks traceability claims.

evidence.note: R10 defines the required evidence pointer object shape including entity_id|null
AT10 pass criteria requires evidence pointers include entity_id|null and RFC6901 json_pointer
Decision evidence pointer instance includes non-standard fields and omits entity_id
Synthesis warning evidence pointer instance also uses non-standard fields and omits entity_id

defects.label: blocker
defects.summary: Stage sequencing mismatch: tool policy requires PatchApply for repo mutation (and Validate forbids repo_write), but milestones and the chosen O1 dataflow jump Generate→Validate with no explicit PatchApply boundary. This creates an undefined 'what code is being validated' state and breaks the determinism/audit model.

evidence.note: PatchApply stage is the only stage allowing repo_write via patch_apply
Validate stage denies repo_write and does not allow patch_apply
M3 Generate depends_on M2 and is followed by M4 Validation; no PatchApply milestone is present
Chosen dataflow omits an explicit patch-apply step/stage between patchset creation and validation

defects.label: blocker
defects.summary: Hard-gate id_integrity failure: deliverable IDs do not match required deliverable ID convention (validator reports all M*-D* deliverable ids invalid). Fix requires renaming many deliverable IDs (ID-bearing changes) across milestones; this should be rerouted to the synthesizer/plan-writer for consistent ID regeneration rather than ad-hoc patching.

evidence.note: id_integrity violations list: Deliverable id does not match DL# for M1-D1..M7-D3
Milestones contain deliverables with M*-D* IDs that trigger validator failure

defects.label: fix
defects.summary: Architecture chosen/key_design_decisions entries are missing explicit linkage to decision_log (validator reports 'Decision reference missing' for multiple items). Add DEC# references (non-ID-bearing string edits) to improve traceability and satisfy decision-reference checks.

evidence.note: Key design decision strings currently have no DEC# references
Validator lists multiple 'Decision reference missing' violations for key_design_decisions

patch.value: Linear state machine (C1) enforces strict stage ordering with no parallelism; only one stage is active at any time, maximizing determinism and auditability. (DEC1)
Big-bang milestone strategy: all deliverables converge into a single freeze event; no partial freezes or incremental releases. (DEC2)

High HITL strictness: every escalation trigger (ChangeRequest, forbidden-path access, secrets detection, retry budget exhaustion, waiver requests, tool permission expansion) requires human approval before proceeding. (DEC3)

Repair loops (C8 → C6) are bounded by orchestrator-enforced iteration caps and operation caps; smallest-passing-repair selection uses deterministic tie-breakers (fewest ops → fewest bytes → first-generated). (DEC4)
Secrets scanning runs at every checkpoint boundary and before freeze; any detection blocks persistence and triggers HITL. (DEC3)

defects.summary: Tool policy prohibits canonical artifact writes required by milestones: Intake stage allows only non-canonical writes but M1 requires canonical run_manifest/event_log/stage_handoff; Review stage denies all writes but M5 requires review_findings.json and stage_handoff.

evidence.note: Intake restrictions allow only non-canonical writes
M1 requires canonical run_manifest/event_log initialization

M5 requires review_findings.json emission

payload.reroute_reason: At minimum, the id_integrity hard-gate failure on deliverable ID convention requires sweeping ID-bearing renames across milestones/deliverables; per workflow rules this should be regenerated/rewritten by the synthesizer rather than patched locally. Additional blockers (tool policy contradictions; evidence pointer schema mismatch; stage sequencing) can likely be patched, but the ID-convention failure alone warrants reroute.
